Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Preserve every other cell, including the original motif and zeros/background at non-motif positions inside the bounding box. Do not assume flood-fill or neighbor propagation: test motif translations when the grid visually consists of noisy background plus one seed object.
3. Use a small script to enumerate translations and construct output grids when manual scanning is error-prone. Validate by matching all demonstrated changed/unchanged cells; account for seed shape, legal translations within bounds, and any rotation/reflection only if supported by demonstrations.
4. When full-width and full-height separator lines partition a grid into equal tiles and the output dimensions match the tile layout, map each tile to one output cell. Use demonstrations to identify which in-tile feature or count determines the output; do not assume every unusual cell or single marker is positive. For the task pattern with color-8 separators, 2×3 tiles containing mostly color 3 and occasional color 2, emit 1 for a tile with at least two 2s and 3 otherwise.
5. For sparse colored diagonal markers on a zero field, identify the invariant of their parallel lines: constant row−column for down-right diagonals, or row+column for down-left diagonals. Demonstrations may show that the output fills the whole grid with a periodic color sequence indexed by that invariant. Use zero-based row/column coordinates and verify the sign convention against observed output: for down-right stripes, `column−row` indexes the phase; for down-left stripes, `row+column` does. Infer the smallest plausible period and color per phase by checking which candidate periods avoid assigning different colors to the same residue; use demo output to establish the complete mapping when available. Do not assume the marker positions alone give every residue's color; use output examples to establish the complete mapping.

It may be a solid suffix or only selected motif-phase positions. Color only the confirmed missing continuation cells; preserve the existing motif and unrelated cells. Check the candidate against every demo's changed and unchanged cells, and select repeated copies from that evidence—not from rightmost zeros or suffix length alone.
7. Choose exactly one legal action. Request a demonstration only when its expected information is worth its cost; submit when the rule is adequately supported; finish only after the instance is over. Account for the stated scoring penalties and caps.
8. Reply with only the action JSON object and do not call unrelated tools.
